name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

ingredients.buy: 12 oz (2 1/3 of the 5.2 oz packages), crumbled

prose.intro_html: Here is a weeknight truth worth putting in a frame: the pasta cooks itself. You dump raw penne, cubed chicken, peas, and artichokes into one dish, pour a blender sauce over the whole thing, and the oven handles the rest. No pot of boiling water, no colander, no second pan waiting in the sink to judge you. Cottage cheese and Boursin carry the sauce, so it drinks like something far richer than the ledger says it should be. And the ledger is the point here. Each of the 14 servings lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, which is a serious plate of dinner for what it costs to make.
prose.shop_smart:
• Penne is the base. You need 1 lb 12 oz dry, so grab a box and a bit, or two boxes if your store only sells the standard one-pound size. Any short tube shape works if penne is out.
  • Boneless skinless chicken breast, 3 1/2 lb, is the anchor. A family pack is the friend here. Cube it into 1-inch pieces at home so it cooks evenly in the bake.
  • Cottage cheese does the creamy work: 4 2/3 cups, which is about a 2 lb 5 oz tub. Full-fat or low-fat both blend smooth, so buy what your store stocks.
  • Boursin Garlic and Fine Herbs comes in 5.2 oz rounds. The build wants 12 oz, which is 2 1/3 of them, so put three in the cart and you will have a little left for toast.
  • Artichoke hearts, 1 lb 4 oz drained, runs about 2 1/3 of the standard 14 oz cans. Buy three cans, drain and chop.
  • Frozen green peas keep the cost low and the color bright. You need 2 1/3 cups, so one bag covers it with room to spare.
  • Grate the parmesan fresh from a block if you can. It melts smoother and tastes cleaner than the shaker stuff, and this dish gives it a starring golden crust.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease your baking vessel. Because this is scaled to 14 servings, use a large deep roasting pan, or split everything evenly across two 9x13 dishes. One standard 9x13 will not hold this much pasta and chicken, and you need room to submerge the noodles.

Build the sauce in a blender or food processor. Combine the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt, and blend until smooth. Pour in the chicken broth and blend again until it is completely incorporated. Do not panic when it looks thin. It is supposed to be very thin, because that liquid is what cooks the raw pasta.

Now the fun part, which is barely any work at all. Spread the dry penne across the bottom, then scatter the cubed chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the blended sauce over everything and press the pasta down so it is fully submerged. Every noodle that sticks up dry will stay hard, so tuck them all under.

Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull it out, take off the foil, and give it a good stir. The pasta should be slightly undercooked at this point. Top with the freshly grated parmesan and return it, uncovered, for another 5 to 10 minutes until golden. You can nudge the temperature up to help the top brown. If the pasta already feels al dente, just add the parmesan and let it rest.

Rest the finished dish for at least 10 minutes before you touch it. Finish with chopped fresh parsley or basil, and serve.
prose.portion_html: We portion by weight, not by eyeball, because the eyeball always cheats in somebody's favor. Set your empty container on the scale and zero it out, then weigh the full casserole and divide that number by 14. That is your target weight per container. Scoop to that number every time, cutting through chicken, pasta, and artichoke so each box gets a fair share of the good stuff, not one lucky container hoarding all the chicken. Fourteen even portions, and the macros on the label are the macros in the box.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is where the no-boil trick pays you back twice. One dish, one blender, and pantry-friendly players like cottage cheese and frozen peas keep this at ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is a full dinner with {{protein}} grams of protein for less than most drive-thru value menus, and you are not eating it in a parking lot.
prose.upsell_html: If this is the kind of math you want running your kitchen, that is the whole idea behind Thrifty Crew. Every recipe is costed, portioned, and built to feed you well without robbing you. Membership runs a dollar a month, which is roughly the change under your couch cushion, and it keeps recipes like this one coming.

head.description: A dump-and-bake no-boil chicken pasta casserole with artichokes and peas, scaled to 14 high-protein meal-prep servings. The raw penne cooks right in a creamy cottage cheese and Boursin sauce, no pot of boiling water required.

steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and grease a large deep roasting pan, or two 9x13 dishes, since this is scaled to 14 servings.
Blend the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt until smooth, then blend in the chicken broth. The sauce will be very thin, which is correct.
Spread the dry penne on the bottom, scatter the cubed chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over it, then pour the sauce over everything and press the pasta down so it is fully submerged.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 40 minutes. Uncover, stir, top with freshly grated parmesan, and return uncovered for 5 to 10 minutes until golden, bumping the heat if needed.
Rest at least 10 minutes, finish with chopped fresh parsley or basil, and serve or portion into containers.
